topic: Can satellite orbital configurations optimize ML-based QoS by reducing propagation delays for latency-sensitive traffic classes?
consensus_response: Satellite orbital configurations can be optimized to reduce propagation delays and improve the quality of service (QoS) for latency-sensitive traffic classes. By incorporating real-time satellite link characteristics, including latency and jitter, into ML-based QoS mechanisms, these systems can dynamically adjust path selection to balance performance with budget constraints. This approach ensures optimal paths are chosen for all traffic flows, improving the Quality of Experience (QoE) for latency-sensitive applications in converged satellite and terrestrial networks.
reference_context: The reference context highlights the limitations of current QoS mechanisms, such as IntServ and QoS-OSPF, which neglect high fixed latencies of satellite links. It emphasizes the need to consider link characteristics like latency and jitter during path selection and admission control to provide optimal QoS guarantees in converged satellite and terrestrial networks.
